findings.title: Accidental git submodule entry added to repository
findings.body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951...`, i.e. a gitlink to the base Sentry commit. No `.gitmodules` entry is included and the change is unrelated to the feature. This will leave a broken/empty submodule in checkouts and can break CI or tooling that recursively updates submodules. Remove the gitlink from the PR.

findings.title: Tests assign to read-only DRF Request.GET and fail in setUp
findings.body: `rest_framework.request.Request.GET` is a read-only property proxying the underlying Django request. Assigning `self.request.GET = QueryDict('')` in `setUp` (and later in the test methods) raises `AttributeError`, so the whole new test module fails before any assertion. Build requests with query strings via `RequestFactory().get('/?query=...')` or mutate `self.request._request.GET` instead.

findings.title: Naive query substring check applies upsampling to non-error queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats the presence of the literal substring `event.type:error` as proof that the query is error-only. Negated filters such as `!event.type:error`, mixed filters such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or quoted text containing that substring all match. When the dataset is `discover`, this makes the endpoint replace `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)` for queries that also contain transactions or are transaction-only; transactions have no sample weight, so results are wrong or the query fails. Parse the query conditions (or at least handle negation/mixed event.type filters) instead of using `in`.

findings.title: New upsampled_count function is publicly exposed without gating
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is registered in the discover dataset's function converter without `private=True` (unlike neighboring internal functions). This makes it available to user-supplied `yAxis`/query strings even when the project is not allowlisted or the dataset is transactions. In those cases `sample_weight` is absent/meaningless, so users can get ClickHouse errors or counts that bypass the eligibility logic that the helper is supposed to enforce. Mark the function private or otherwise restrict it to the transformed internal path.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility ignores the scoped dataset and rewritten query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` computes eligibility with the closure's original `dataset` and with `request.GET['query']`, not with the `scoped_dataset` and `query` parameters that are actually executed. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is called with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a rewritten query (e.g. `errors_only_query`), but the check still sees the original dataset (such as `metrics_enhanced_performance`) and original user query. As a result, error-only split queries are not upsampled, and internal query rewrites cannot alter the decision. Pass the actual dataset/query into the eligibility check.

findings.title: Top events ordering still uses raw count while displayed counts are upsampled
findings.body: Only `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` are transformed to `upsampled_count()`; `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` is passed through unchanged. For a `topEvents` query ordered by `-count()`, the top N groups are therefore selected by raw event count while the returned series shows upsampled counts. If sample rates differ between groups, the API can return the wrong groups/order. Transform the orderby (and any count references in equations) consistently for top events.
